on 14 August, 2024
 1
 The Honourable Sri Justice E.V.Venugopal
 Criminal Petition No.2650 Of 2019
Order:

The present Criminal Petition is filed seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.33 in C.C.No.10 of 2017 on the file of the learned XVI Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally, at Miyapur (for short, "the trial Court") for the offences punishable under Sections 120B, 420 of I.P.C., Section 66 of IP Act, Sections 8 and 10 of AP Public Examinations (Prevention of Malpractices and Unfair Means) Act, 1997.

entities.text: XVI Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally, at Miyapur
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: AP Public Examinations (Prevention of Malpractices and Unfair Means) Act, 1997
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
2. Heard Mr.Akkam Eshwar, learned counsel for the petitioner and Ms.S.Madhavi, learned Assistant Public Prosecutor appearing for respondent No.2-State.
3.

The brief facts of the case are that on 04.04.2016, respondent No.1/de facto complainant filed a complaint before the Cyber Crime Police Station stating that the petitioner/accused No.33 and others involved in mass mal- practicing through electronic devices to help the candidates who are writing Railway erstwhile Group-D RRC recruitment examinations.

Basing on the said facts, Crime No.42 of 2016 was registered against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 120B,
420 of I.P.C., Section 66 of IP Act, Sections 8 and 10 of AP Public Examinations (Prevention of Malpractices and Unfair Means) Act, 1997.

entities.text: AP Public Examinations (Prevention of Malpractices and Unfair Means) Act, 1997
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that, there are no allegations levelled against the petitioner in the entire charge sheet except the confessional statement made by accused No.1 stating that he committed the alleged offences along with the petitioner and others.
He further stated that the petitioner never used any electronic device and no such device is stated to have been recovered from him.
Therefore, he submitted that except the statement of the co-accused, no specific allegation is attributed against him and seeks to set aside the impugned proceedings.
5. Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor contended that unless and until a full-fledged trial is conducted, the truth cannot be elicited.
Therefore, she seeks to dismiss the Criminal Petition.

6. This Court vide order dated 12.06.2019 granted interim stay of all further proceedings in C.C.No.10 of 2017 on the file of the learned XVI Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally, at Miyapur insofar as the petitioner/accused No.33 is concerned.

entities.text: XVI Metropolitan Magistrate, Kukatpally, at Miyapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Later, the interim order was extended from time to time.

7. Having regard to the submissions made by both the learned counsel, this Court is of the opinion Peketi Rajashekar vs G. Naveen Kumar on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108580972/
1 that the matter requires adjudication at length and only upon conclusion of a full-fledged trial, the truth would come to light.

entities.text: Peketi Rajashekar vs G. Naveen Kumar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, this Court is not inclined to entertain the Criminal Petition at this premature stage and the Criminal Petition is liable to be dismissed.
8. Accordingly, this Criminal Petition is dismissed.

However, the appearance of the petitioner,
before the trial Court, is dispensed with on each and every adjournment.
However, he shall appear before the trial Court as and when specifically required.
Miscellaneous Petitions, pending if any, shall stand closed.

_____________________ E.V.VENUGOPAL, J Date: 14.08.2024 ESP Peketi Rajashekar vs G. Naveen Kumar on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108580972/
